dedupe_keys.name: access network traffic profiles from 3 129 real german broadband connections 2024 to 2025

description: Researchers of Technische Hochschule Mittelhessen and the Universität der Bundeswehr München publish aggregated daily traffic profiles of residential broadband access connections in Germany, from a paper at the Optical Fiber Communication Conference (OFC) 2026. The source data are data-rate time series from 3,129 access connections of three established German network operators, recorded in 2024 and 2025 at 1 to 10 second resolution for one to two weeks each. Users were clustered by k-means (three clusters, validated by bootstrap) on mean throughput, upload ratio and activity level, separately for weekdays and weekends; the dataset gives mean profiles per cluster and day type at one-minute resolution and Fourier series coefficients that approximate them. Coverage: Germany, three operators, 2024 to 2025. Format and access: small CSV files and a ZIP of profiles with a README, free of charge under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: aggregated profiles, not raw series; the operators, regions and access technologies are not identified; the Fourier fit is weaker for upstream traffic. Simulation uses: realistic time-varying demand of access networks for capacity planning, energy and resilience studies of fixed broadband and for load on power supply of network equipment. Related records: the CESNET time series give backbone traffic; the Breitbandatlas gives German coverage.
